result_text:
Folders whose names start with `mock` or `__mock` now count as mock-resources (test) code, whatever follows, at any depth and with either path separator.

**Change:** `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (around line 393). The two folder rules were `.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`. They are now:
- `(.*[/\\])?__mock[^/\\]*[/\\].*`
- `(.*[/\\])?mock[^/\\]*[/\\].*`

The `[^/\\]*` part lets the rest of the folder name be anything except a separator, so punctuation and non-ASCII characters are covered. The separator classes make both `/` and `\` work. Matching stays inside one folder name, so `remock/`, `demo/` and files named `mock.java` or `mockery.java` don't match. The optional leading group also catches a top-level `mock/` folder. I left the `mockapi`, `[Mm]ocks` and `_mock.*` rules as they were.

**Test:** I added `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java`. It covers the new cases, the folders that were already classified as test, and the negative cases. The new test passes (3/3). The full `codeanalyzer` module run passed with 333 tests, 0 failures, 3 skipped.

I did not commit.
